newsitem.title: INDIA: Barclays Bank cuts Indian prime lending rate.
newsitem.headline: Barclays Bank cuts Indian prime lending rate.

text.p: Barclays Bank said on Friday it will cut its Indian prime lending rate effective May 1, 1997.
The new prime lending rate will be 16.25 percent per annum for cash credit and 16.0 percent for other loans, down from 17.50 percent earlier, a bank official said.
The spread above the prime rate will be 4.0 percent.
The bank also revised its deposit rates, effective April 16.
The new rates are 7.5 percent for 60 days to 180 days, 9.0 percent for 180 days to one year, 10.75 percent for one to two years and 11.0 percent for two to three years.
The following are the new rates for NRE (non-resident external) and NRNR (non-resident non-repatriable) deposits.
Six months to one year 9.0 percent, one to two years 11.25 percent and two to three years 11.25 percent.
